name: Golden Beer
trait: Doubles every dispatch payout while it sits in your bag
summary: Mazzul's stash of premium beer. Holding it doubles the main rewards of every Greymane dispatch: Camp Funds, food, timber and the rest, on every repeat cycle. Church Blessings multiply on top of it.

return.basis: Doubles every dispatch, but dispatch pays in Camp Funds: the ≈7,000 → ≈14,000 security run is 7 → 14 Silver at the donation rate.

effort.basis: Passive once owned: no activation, no timer, no upkeep.

setup.basis: Main story Chapter 8, the Demeniss noble houses in order up to House Byron, then the Mazzul boss fight.

scale.basis: Applies to every dispatch you run, and to each repeat cycle.

requires: Demeniss noble house chains cleared in order through House Elmore

steps: Clear the Demeniss noble house questlines in their fixed order; House Elmore's courts unlock House Byron.
Run House Byron's Dark Justice chain: A Secret Request, then One Step Ahead. Both lead to Burnhand Quarry.
Defeat Mazzul, the Dark Justiciar. You do not have to clear every soldier in the quarry first.
Keep the Golden Beer in your inventory. The effect applies while you hold it.

location: Burnhand Quarry, Demeniss, near the Kingshield Mountains.
notes: Easy difficulty does not change the reward, so lowering it for the Mazzul fight costs nothing.
Special drops such as Abyss Artifacts from ruin dispatches are not doubled.

captures.caption: Quest map — House Byron's One Step Ahead, Demeniss
Item card — Golden Beer: Double Mission Dispatch Rewards

sources.title: How to Get Golden Beer (via Pulse)

costs.label: Price
costs.value: A boss fight and four questlines

watch: Before patch 1.04 the bonus could silently stop applying after a few hours. Check that your next payout shows the doubled figure.
Rare drops are excluded; only the main reward categories double.

name: Church Blessings
trait: +2% per Blessing level, up to +200%, region by region
summary: Donating Camp Funds to a region's church raises its Blessing level. Each level adds 2% to every dispatch reward in that region, permanently, up to +200%. It multiplies with Golden Beer, so put it where your repeat dispatches already run.

return.basis: Up to +200% on dispatch rewards in one region; the rewards are Camp Funds worth 1/1,000 Silver each.

effort.basis: A one-off donation; the bonus is permanent.

setup.basis: About 110,000 Camp Funds for +100% in Hernand — 110 Silver donated.

scale.basis: Each region needs its own donations, so it scales with how many regions you dispatch in.

steps: Pick the region where your strongest repeat dispatches run.
Open that region's church and donate Camp Funds to raise its Blessing level.
Keep raising the region you already dispatch in before starting a new one.

location: Each region's church, for example the Church of Hernand.
notes: The donation comes out of camp money (Carl's pool), not Kliff's own Silver.

captures.caption: Church screen — Church of Hernand, Blessings on Hernand

sources.title: Church Donations: How Conversion Bonuses Work

watch: The bonus only applies to dispatches in the same region.

name: Estate Security
area: Hillside, Oakenshield, Azerian and Sungrove manors
trait: Food in, Camp Funds out, on repeat
summary: Greymanes guard a manor and bring back Camp Funds. It is the base of the dispatch engine: it costs food, it repeats, and Golden Beer and Blessings multiply it. Payouts in published screenshots run from 1.8K on a basic Hillside run to 13K at Azerian Manor.

return.basis: 1.8K to 13K Camp Funds per run in guide screenshots — 2 to 13 Silver at the donation rate.

effort.basis: Set it to Repeat and it re-queues itself while food lasts.

setup.basis: Comrades with the Escort skill, a stock of food, and a camp at level 2 for the Dispatch Coordinator.

scale.basis: Several manors run at once; each one multiplies with Beer and Blessings.

steps: Talk to Ross at camp, or open Mission Dispatch from the world map.
Pick a manor's Estate Security mission and assign comrades; Escort specialists raise the payout.
Choose Repeat so the crew re-queues when it returns.
Keep a food dispatch running beside it so the queue never stops on an empty larder.

location: Hillside Manor and Oakenshield Manor in Hernand; Azerian and Sungrove manors further afield.
notes: A mission that costs more food than your farms make will stall the whole repeat queue.

captures.caption: Dispatch screen — Azerian Manor estate security, 13K reward in 7 hours
Dispatch screen — Hillside Manor estate security, 1.8K reward in 17 hours

watch: The wiki notes auto-repeat runs paying about half of a buffed manual run (about 15,000 against 30,000) because of a repeat bug; compare your own payouts.

name: Supply Dispatches
trait: Keeps the money missions fed
summary: Quarries, fishing docks, farms and logging camps return food, stone and timber. They pay nothing you can spend at a merchant, but Estate Security eats food and castles, ships and research eat materials. A balanced set of these keeps every money dispatch on Repeat.

return.basis: Pays food and materials, not money.

effort.basis: Runs on Repeat.

setup.basis: Open from the start of camp management; generic workers can fill the slots.

scale.basis: Runs many at once; Grey-0 workers fill the routine slots.

steps: Run at least one food mission (fishing at Rodbel or Nas River docks, or farming) for every food-hungry money mission.
Add quarry and logging missions for the stone and timber that castles, ships and research need.
Measure the net change after a cycle: if food falls, add a producer or drop the weakest consumer.

location: Karin, Perwin and Crimson Mountains quarries; Rodbel and Nas River fishing docks; Dewhaven logging camp.

captures.caption: World map — Karin Quarry
Dispatch screen — Rodbel Fishing Dock freshwater fishing, 1.4K reward
Dispatch screen — small-scale mining, 2.4K reward

watch: Demeniss quarry runs cap at 3,000 stone until regional reputation reaches 50.

name: Excavation Dispatches
trait: The biggest single dispatch payouts on record
summary: Excavation and exploration missions at ruins pay larger lumps of Camp Funds than manor security: The Games Wiki records 37,000 per Tinkerton excavation and 20,000 at Acroser Village. Ruin digs at Timeworn and Bordig also turn up rare items. Patch 1.06 made stronghold excavations repeatable.

return.basis: 37,000 Camp Funds per Tinkerton completion — 37 Silver at the donation rate — plus rare items.

effort.basis: Repeatable at strongholds since 1.06.

setup.basis: Needs comrades with the right specialist skills; Explorer slots cap at five.

scale.basis: Multiplies with Beer and Blessings; limited by specialists and the Explorer cap.

steps: Keep named specialists free for excavation; give routine slots to Grey-0 or hired workers.
Dispatch to the excavation sites and check each one for the Repeat prompt; not every ruin has it.

location: Tinkerton, Acroser Village, and the Timeworn and Bordig ruins.

captures.caption: Dispatch screen — Serpent Shrine exploration with Grey-0 crew

sources.title: Farming Guide: Gold and Abyss Gear

watch: Check the Repeat prompt mission by mission; the wiki warns that not every ruin qualifies.

name: Grey-0 Workers
area: Marni's Steel Armory, near Mount Benos
trait: Mecha workers that fill the routine slots
summary: Grey-0 mecha workers take the ordinary positions on dispatches so your named Greymanes can lead the skill-gated ones, and they lift the roster past its cap of about 37 comrades. More workers mean more missions running at once. They also make a losing queue drain food and funds faster.

return.basis: Adds capacity; pays nothing itself.

effort.basis: Built by a dispatch of their own.

setup.basis: Chapter 10, the Chaya Research at Dewhaven, Marni's Steel Armory liberated, then 10,000 Camp Funds and camp stock per worker.

scale.basis: Every worker opens another slot on another mission.

requires: Chaya Research complete at the Dewhaven Research Institute

steps: At Dewhaven Keep in south-western Delesyia, finish the Electricity – Movement Conversion Mechanism Research, then the Chaya Research. Enter without a mask: the guards attack masked visitors.
Return the Chaya to the Research Assistant at Windrose Farm; the research completes about 8 in-game hours later.
Liberate Marni's Steel Armory by defeating the Mechanicus.
Open the Armory's Missions tab and choose Craft Mecha Worker with two comrades assigned, one an Engineer.
Put the workers on routine positions; keep specialists for excavation, facilities and crew roles.

location: Marni's Steel Armory, central Delesyia near Mount Benos; research at Dewhaven Keep.
notes: Add workers only to a portfolio whose food and funds already balance.

captures.caption: Dispatch screen — Grey-0 workers filling a mission crew

sources.title: Grey-0 Mecha Workers: Unlock, Craft, and Deploy
How to Create Grey-0 Mecha Workers

watch: Workers do not make a losing mission profitable; they make it lose faster.
Guides disagree on output: one worker per about 4 hours (All Things How, Console Pulse) against 1–3 every 3 hours (The Games Wiki).

name: Timberham Sawmill
trait: The first lease: 15,000 and a working business
summary: The DLC's first business. A notice on the Hernand board leads to the lease, and the quest that follows teaches workstations, pricing and popularity. In one published screenshot a young sawmill earned 48,422 Camp Funds across 40 hours open on 4,200 daily wages; finishing it opens leasing everywhere else.

return.basis: 48,422 Camp Funds over 40 hours open in a guide screenshot — 48 Silver at the donation rate; a 7-hour day ran at a loss.

effort.basis: Earns while you are away, but stock, workstations and prices need setting up.

setup.basis: 15,000 lease and four comrades, ideally Logging and Crafting at level 3.

scale.basis: One building; its popularity levels raise customers and unlock recipes.

routes.label: The Stilled Saw → The Saw Turns Again
steps: Read the Timberham Sawmill notice on the Hernand board to start Renewed Vitality.
Open the map's Facilities tab, select the sawmill and sign the 15,000 lease.
Assign four Greymanes, ideally with level 3 Logging and Crafting, and match workstations to the staff you have.
Price low until Popularity Level 3: give customers fair prices, enable Wood Synergy, sell 10 plank items.
Reaching Popularity Level 3 completes the quest and opens leasing at the other facilities.

location: Timberham, Hernand region.
notes: Workers assigned to a facility cannot go on dispatches or crew a ship.

captures.caption: Sawmill open — 104 customers, 48,422 earned over 40 hours
Sawmill open — 18,094 earned in 7 hours, 25,160 daily upkeep
Setting up — placing installables in the yard

watch: Upkeep and wages are charged daily. A young shop can run at a loss, as the 7-hour screenshot shows.
Vulkk writes the lease as 15,000 Copper and Xbox Play as 15,000 Camp Funds: the same sum, since Camp Funds are counted in copper. Donated, it is 15 Silver.
Patch 2.04.02 fixed a bug that inflated facility earnings; earnings figures from before October 30 overstate the real rate.

name: Facility Leases
area: 18 facilities: sawmills, restaurants, smithies, tailor's shops
trait: Eighteen businesses that earn while you explore
summary: After the sawmill, 17 more facilities can be leased: sawmills, restaurants, smithies and tailor's shops in liberated strongholds. Each needs staff with the matching skill. Players have reported around a million Camp Funds a day from one shop, but those reports predate the fix to inflated facility earnings.

return.basis: About 1M Camp Funds a day from one shop — 1,000 Silver at the donation rate — in a player report from before the 2.04.02 earnings fix.

effort.basis: Passive while open; prices, stock and popularity tasks need attention.

setup.basis: A lease, a liberated stronghold, its regional faction quest finished, and staff with the matching skill.

scale.basis: Up to 18 businesses at once; each levels up with popularity.

requires: Stronghold liberated and its faction quest finished
Staff with Cooking, Smithing, Tailoring or Woodworking

steps: Look for a purple lease notice in town, or open the map's Facilities tab.
Choose the business your roster can staff: Cooking for a restaurant, Smithing for a smithy, Tailoring for a tailor's shop.
Check the lease cost and your Camp Funds balance, then lease from the facility's icon.
Keep prices low while levelling popularity, then raise them at the top level.

location: Restaurant at Vellua; smithy at Zargan Tankworks; tailor's shops and further sawmills listed in the Facilities tab.
notes: Skilled staff work faster and draw higher wages; keep cheaper staff until revenue covers them.
Popularity levels unlock wealthier customers, better recipes, equipment and blueprints.

captures.caption: Smithy — “the finest blacksmith in town”
Restaurant — a cook at work

sources.title: Players are sharing their best money-making grinds

watch: Patch 2.04.02 fixed a bug that inflated facility earnings. The million-a-day reports came out around launch; treat them as a ceiling.
A facility worker is out of the dispatch and ship-crew pool.
Its Potential tier is Income, not Fortune: the tier list counts no figure a later patch cut, and the post-fix figures (the Timberham Sawmill's) come to well under a Gold Bar's worth a day.

name: Castles
area: Drakesfall Castle and Flame Knights' Castle
trait: A home for the Greymanes that pays nothing back
summary: Two castles can be claimed after Journey's End and rebuilt by a 20-comrade crew over 15 in-game days. They give room to furnish, store resources and house fighters, and they host merchants. No source reports income from either, so on this route they are something to buy with surplus.

return.basis: No source reports castle income.

effort.basis: A single long dispatch per castle.

setup.basis: Flame Knights' Castle takes 100,000 funds, 10,000 weapons, 10,000 provisions, 40,000 stone and 40,000 wood plus 20 comrades.

scale.basis: Two castles; nothing compounds.

routes.label: Drakesfall Castle
steps: Clear Drakesfall Castle's occupants to start Shield of Hernand; Duke Celeste awards the castle.
Select the castle on the map, open Missions and dispatch Castle Construction: 20 comrades and 30,000 funds.
Wait out the 15 in-game days.

routes.label: Flame Knights' Castle
steps: Play Damiane's From the Ashes questline through Path of the Politician.
Rebuild with 20 comrades, 100,000 funds, 10,000 weapons, 10,000 provisions, 40,000 stone and 40,000 wood; it takes 15 in-game days.

location: Drakesfall Castle in Hernand; Flame Knights' Castle in western Demeniss.

captures.caption: World map — Flame Knights' Castle, Demeniss
World map — Drakesfall Castle, Hernand
Furnishing — placing installables inside a castle

watch: Twenty comrades leave your dispatch queue for 15 days; stock food first.

name: Small Greymane Ship
trait: The quest-built ship: the Small Hernandian's 14 cargo slots without its 40,000 price
summary: A Call from Beyond the Horizon has you build your first ship at a port: five comrades, a 12-hour dispatch and a list of camp materials. The result has the same 14 inventory slots as the 40,000 Small Hernandian Ship, so building it lets you skip that purchase and save toward the Medium.

return.basis: A vessel: it pays through the trade, bounties and island dispatches it opens.

effort.basis: One 12-hour dispatch; sleeping advances the clock.

setup.basis: Five comrades with the skill requirement met, and 600, 600, 1,200 and 10,000 of the listed materials.

scale.basis: 14 inventory slots and 5,100 health.

requires: Howling Hill expanded until A Wider World unlocks
Five comrades, including the Engineering skill requirement

routes.label: A Wider World
steps: Select a port on the map and start Shipbuilding from its Missions menu.
Assign five comrades and meet the skill and material requirements.
Wait or sleep through the 12 in-game hours.
Crew it at the Ship Manager — First Mate, Rigger and Lookout are required to leave port — then follow Where the Wind Blows.

location: Vellua port, Grace Estate.

captures.caption: Dispatch screen — Small Shipbuilding, 12 hours
Tutorial — Shipbuilding from a port's Missions menu

DLC Shipbuilding Guide: All Ships and Upgrades
How to Unlock and Upgrade Ships

figures.value: 14 slots, same as the 40,000 Small Hernandian

watch: The three crew roles the departure check names are First Mate, Rigger and Lookout; without them the ship stays in port.

name: Fleetmaster Ships
area: Fleetmasters at Vellua, Demeniss and Delesyia
trait: 2,000 to 6,000,000: buy cargo space, not the next size up
summary: Fleetmasters sell four ships for Camp Funds. Inventory is what a trading ship is for: the Rowboat holds 6, the Small Hernandian 14, the Medium 22 and the Large 36. With the quest ship already at 14, the Medium (1.2M) is the first purchase that adds capacity — and since 2.01 1.2M Camp Funds is 1,200 donated Silver, and the Large's 6M is 6,000.

return.basis: Vessels pay through cargo and the routes they open.

effort.basis: A purchase; no build time.

setup.basis: 1,200,000 Camp Funds for the Medium and 6,000,000 for the Large: 1,200 and 6,000 Silver donated.

scale.basis: The Large carries 36 slots and 10,000 health — the most capacity in the game.

steps: Skip the 40,000 Small Hernandian Ship if you built the Small Greymane Ship: both hold 14.
Buy the Large Hernandian Ship at 6,000,000 — 6,000 donated Silver, twelve Gold Bars — once you hold that much spare: 36 slots.
Short of that, the Medium at 1,200,000 (1,200 Silver) gives 22 slots.
Buy from Hopkins at Vellua (Grace Estate) or the Fleetmasters at Demeniss and Delesyia.

location: Hopkins at Vellua, Grace Estate; Fleetmasters at Demeniss and Delesyia.

captures.caption: Fleetmaster — all four ships and prices, Large Hernandian selected
At sea — a Hernandian ship under striped sails

name: Crew and Outfitting
trait: Gunners for cannons, Carpenters for hulls, Deckhands for islands
summary: Crew roles decide what a ship can do. First Mate, Rigger and Lookout are required to leave port; Gunners fire the cannons, Carpenters repair faster, and Deckhands work the island dispatches. Outfitters at Demeniss and Delesyia sell sails, sterns, figureheads and guns. A Fleetmaster will retrieve a lost ship for a fee: 19,880 in one screenshot.

return.basis: Upgrades protect cargo and open combat and island work; no direct income.

effort.basis: Roles change only in port.

setup.basis: Comrades for every role, plus outfitter prices.

scale.basis: A crewed, armed ship can take pirate bounties and island missions.

steps: Assign First Mate, Rigger and Lookout at the Ship Manager before boarding.
Add a Gunner before fitting cannons, and a Carpenter if you expect damage.
Keep Deckhands for island dispatches.
Buy parts from the Ship Outfitters at Demeniss and Delesyia.

location: Ship Managers at any port; Ship Outfitters at Demeniss and Delesyia.

captures.caption: Ship Manager — crew roles: First Mate, Lookout, Carpenter, Gunner, Deckhands
Fleetmaster — repair and retrieve a ship for 19,880

name: Island Pioneering
area: Auronui Island, then Samora and Winding Island
trait: Three comrades, twelve hours, a new anchorage
summary: Pioneering an island sends three comrades on a 12-hour dispatch from its anchorage. A pioneered island gives an anchorage, ship teleportation, new missions and new shops. Auronui comes first, and its buried treasure holds the Ship Teleportation Device blueprint. No source yet documents island upgrade tiers or island income.

return.basis: No source documents island income yet.

effort.basis: One dispatch per island, started from the anchorage.

setup.basis: A crewed ship with Deckhands, three free comrades and the mission's materials.

scale.basis: Each island adds missions, shops and a teleport point.

routes.label: Auronui Island
steps: Sail south past the coast near Vellua to Auronui during A Wider World.
Keep the ship inside the island's marked Anchorage area.
Open Map → Facilities, select the Anchorage marker and start the Pioneer mission with three comrades.
After the 12 hours, return to the same Anchorage and choose Complete Mission.

location: Auronui Island, in the southern sea beyond Vellua.
notes: Landing on the island does not complete pioneering; the dispatch does.
Islands after Auronui: Samora, held by pirates, and Winding Island.

name: Pailune Reconstruction
trait: Rebuild Kliff's hometown; the final camp depends on it
summary: Rebuilding Pailune follows Chapter 7 and needs camp level 2: donate the listed materials and wait out about two days and six hours. A finished main story does not finish this rebuild, and the move to the final camp checks for it.

return.basis: Unlocks the final camp; no direct income.

effort.basis: Donations and a wait.

setup.basis: Material donations from the camp pool.

scale.basis: A one-time project.

steps: Check Pailune's stronghold summary for the reconstruction requirements.
Donate the requested materials.
Wait out the rebuild, about two in-game days and six hours.

location: Pailune city, north of Hernand.

captures.caption: Stronghold summary — Pailune

name: Pailune Camp
trait: Double the farm and ranch, 1,000 storage slots
summary: Moving the Greymanes to Pailune is the last camp upgrade. Twice the farm and ranch space means more food for the dispatch queue, and 1,000 Private Storage slots hold cargo between runs. It needs the full main story, every Scattered Embers and Grounds of the Sunrise quest, a rebuilt Pailune and a fully upgraded Howling Hill.

return.basis: Indirect: doubled farm and ranch space feeds food-hungry dispatches.

effort.basis: A long quest checklist, then one move.

setup.basis: At least 31 Scattered Embers and 37 Grounds of the Sunrise quests, plus a full Howling Hill.

scale.basis: Doubles food capacity for the dispatch engine.

requires: All Scattered Embers and Grounds of the Sunrise quests
Pailune rebuilt; Howling Hill fully upgraded

routes.label: The Return Home
steps: Make a manual save; the relocation cutscene overwrites the autosave.
Harvest crops, cancel dispatches and empty every camp building's storage.
Talk to Serkis in Hernand Town to take The Return Home.
Return to Howling Hill and step into the camp's centre to trigger the move.

location: Pailune city; the move starts with Serkis in Hernand Town.
notes: After the move, Silver boxes left at Howling Hill count as theft if you take them.

name: Trade Wagons
trait: Buy where it is cheap, drive it where it is not
summary: Patch 1.16 rebuilt trading: 133 Trading Posts, 28 new trade goods, seven Wagon Workshops, live prices on a Trade map tab, and prices that sag when one good floods a market. Packaged goods are bought and sold in Camp Funds: one published run sold 150 Packaged Salt at 563 for 84,450 Camp Funds, a 61,800 margin. At 1,000 Camp Funds to the Silver that load cleared about 62 Silver.

return.basis: A 61,800 Camp Funds margin on one 150-unit Salt load — about 62 Silver at the donation rate.

effort.basis: You drive every run and choose every load.

setup.basis: Brice, an Engineer and the Timberturner Wainwright, after A Rumor in Glenbright Farm.

scale.basis: Packaged goods stack to 10 or 100; supply pressure lowers a price you keep selling into.

requires: Brice recruited through A Rumor in Glenbright Farm
An Engineer for the wagon chain

steps: Open the Trade tab on the world map and filter by good before loading anything.
Find the buyer first, then buy or package the cargo.
Test a route with a small load before sending a full wagon down mountain roads.
Load a return cargo so the wagon never drives back empty.

location: Trading Posts across Pywel; Wagon Workshops in seven towns.
notes: Since 1.16 you can move trade goods between wagon and horse.
Package raw trade goods at camp before loading; only packaged goods sell at Trading Posts.

captures.caption: Trade tab — market prices and filters
Sale — 150 Packaged Salt at 563, 84,450 total

Patch 1.16 raised the cargo lost when a wagon is destroyed or retrieved, or a loaded horse is retrieved.
Selling a lot of one good at one post lowers its price there.

name: Royal Trading Posts
trait: Patch 1.16 multiplied their trade-good prices by four
summary: Royal Trading Posts buy only the packaged goods their court lists, at four times the old price since 1.16, and your wagon now stays after a Royal delivery. One guide found Varnia's Royal post paying 1,000 Camp Funds for Packaged Cheese bought at 118 elsewhere: about 132,000 on a 150-unit load, or 132 Silver at the donation rate.

return.basis: Varnia listed Packaged Cheese at 1,000 Camp Funds against a 118 buy price: about 132 Silver on a 150-unit load.

effort.basis: Long hauls to the court that wants the good.

setup.basis: A working wagon and the right packaged good for each court.

scale.basis: Each court has a purchase limit and supply pressure moves its price.

steps: Open the stronghold's Royal Trading list to see which packaged good the court wants and its limit.
Buy that good where the Trade tab shows it cheapest.
Deliver it, then reload at a nearby post for the next leg.

location: Royal Trading Posts, including Varnia's and the one north of Hernand Castle.

captures.caption: World map — Varnia's Royal Trading Post
Purchase — 150 Packaged Cheese at 118, 17,700 total
Royal Trading list — Packaged Honey at 328, limit 100

Prices move: the guide warns its Varnia price is not a permanent route.

name: Camp Donations
trait: 1 Silver → 1,000 Camp Funds since 2.01
summary: Camp Funds are counted in copper, and since patch 2.01 every copper of Silver you donate to Carl becomes ten: one Silver buys 1,000 Camp Funds and one Gold Bar, exchanged at a bank, buys 500,000. That makes the DLC's Camp Funds prices small in Silver: the 6,000,000 Large Hernandian Ship is 6,000 Silver, twelve Gold Bars.

return.basis: Converts Silver into Camp Funds; earns nothing itself.

effort.basis: One menu at camp.

setup.basis: Available from the start of camp management.

scale.basis: No cap is documented.

steps: Exchange Gold Bars for Silver at a bank: 500 Silver each. A merchant pays about 190.
Talk to Carl at camp and choose Donate Funds.
Donate the Silver you will not spend: each Silver adds 1,000 Camp Funds, and the donation cannot be reversed.
Do not hand Carl a Gold Bar itself: the only measured bar donation is 50,000, from before 2.01, against 500,000 for the same bar as Silver.

location: Carl, the Provisions Keeper, at camp.
notes: Camp Funds are counted in copper: 100 Camp Funds was one Silver before 2.01, 1,000 since.

captures.caption: Bank exchange — 1 Gold Bar ↔ 500 Silver

costs.label: Direction
costs.value: One way: Camp Funds cannot become Silver again

watch: The Games Wiki's 50,000 Camp Funds per donated Gold Bar is the pre-2.01 copper value (500 Silver × 100). Exchange bars for Silver first.
The 1,000-per-Silver rate comes from players who measured it (a mod that reverses the game's own donation, and its notes); Pearl Abyss's patch note says ×10 without a base.

name: Bank Investment
trait: Gold Bars that swing every three in-game days
summary: A 100-Silver Strongbox permit lets you invest Gold Bars at Low (0% to +2%), Medium (−15% to +20%) or High (−50% to +55%) risk. Each cycle rolls about every three in-game days, and the strategy can change only every 15. Only Low cannot lose. Patch 1.16 capped gains and losses at 40 bars a cycle and added Hernand Bonds, which need 100 bars to start.

return.basis: Gold Bars, up to 40 a cycle: with a save before each roll and a reload on a loss, Medium never loses and gains up to +20% every three days. Without one it averages about +2.5%.

effort.basis: Deposit and collect; sleeping speeds the cycle.

setup.basis: A 100-Silver permit and spare Gold Bars.

scale.basis: Capped at 40 bars gained or lost per cycle since 1.16.

routes.label: Gold Bar interest
steps: Buy the Personal Strongbox Permit for 100 Silver at a bank.
Deposit only bars you will not need for gear, recipes or donations.
Choose Low for bars you cannot afford to lose; Medium or High only with a manual save before the roll.
Collect each cycle, about three in-game days.

routes.label: Hernand Bonds
steps: Claim Bank Strongbox converts bars to Hernand Bonds: one Bond is 10 bars.
Bond investing unlocks at 10 Bonds — 100 genuinely spare bars.

location: Any bank in Pywel; Grover in Hernand.
notes: Crude Gold Bars cannot be invested or turned into Bonds.
The Golden Piggy Bank produces Copper Pouches while you are offline.

name: Gold Bar Crafting
area: Witch's Hideout, gold caves, hedgehog trails
trait: 1 Golden Apple + 3 Gold Ore = 1 Gold Bar
summary: A Witch turns one Golden Apple and three Gold Ore into a Gold Bar. The bank pays 500 Silver for it, and that Silver donates as 500,000 Camp Funds. Golden Apples ride on hedgehogs' backs — watch the ground for the glint — and Gold Ore comes from caves such as Silver Wolf Cave.

return.basis: 500 Silver per bar at a bank; supply is bound by hedgehog spawns.

effort.basis: Hunting hedgehogs and mining ore by hand.

setup.basis: The recipe from the bookshelf in the Witch's Hideout south of Pailune.

scale.basis: Bound by hedgehog spawns, which 2.04 reduced.

requires: Gold Bar recipe from the Witch's Hideout, south of Pailune

steps: Take the recipe from the bookshelf inside the Witch's Hideout south of Pailune.
Mine Gold Ore on a cave circuit; Silver Wolf Cave has dense clusters.
Hunt Golden Apple hedgehogs near Grey Rock Dock, the Eastern Hills of Delesyia or Tariv, roughly 16:00 to midnight.
Craft at a Witch, then exchange the bars at a bank for 500 Silver each.

location: Witch's Hideout south of Pailune; Grey Rock Dock in Demeniss; Silver Wolf Cave.
notes: A blacksmith converts 100 Gold Ore into one bar: over thirty times the ore of the Witch recipe.
Never sell a Golden Apple raw (114 Silver) or a Gold Bar to a merchant (about 190).

name: Noble Pickpocketing
trait: Gold Bars lifted from wealthy visitors
summary: Nobles strolling Demeniss Wildlife Park carry Gold Bars. Inspect them with the lantern, pick the ones showing a stacked bar, and lift it with a mask on. One player reports six bars in about 25 minutes: 3,000 Silver at a bank, or 3,000,000 Camp Funds donated.

return.basis: About six Gold Bars in 25 minutes in a player report: 3,000 Silver, the fastest Silver documented here.

effort.basis: Hands-on, target by target.

setup.basis: A mask and a lantern.

scale.basis: Limited by targets and bounty.

steps: Equip a mask before entering the park.
Inspect nobles with the lantern; look for the stacked Gold Bar icon, not a pouch.
Pickpocket, then leave the red witness circle before the next target.
Pay off bounty at a confessional in Hernand Castle town.

location: Demeniss Wildlife Park, about 2,000 metres east of Castle Hernand; a cluster of about 50 nobles in the south-east.

name: Crude Gold Circuit
area: Harpy Nest, Demeniss warehouse and three more caches
trait: 400 bars, 5 Silver each
summary: Five static caches hold roughly 400 Crude Gold Bars, which any merchant buys at 5 Silver: about 2,000 Silver a circuit, or 2,000,000 Camp Funds donated. The Harpy Nest in Pailune alone holds about 150. It is the smallest earner here; run it only when you are passing the caches.

return.basis: About 2,000 Silver per full circuit; the caches take several in-game days to respawn.

effort.basis: A five-stop route by hand.

setup.basis: A bandit mask and an ice-resistance cloak for the Harpy Nest.

scale.basis: Caches respawn after several in-game days.

steps: Equip a bandit mask for the Demeniss warehouse and Delesyia Castle stops, where the bars must be stolen.
Wear ice resistance (+5) at the Harpy Nest in Pailune; hold E to collect everything nearby.
Sell to any merchant at 5 Silver each.

location: Harpy Nest, north-west of the A in Pailune (≈150); Demeniss warehouse north of Flame Knights' Castle (≈80); three more caches.
notes: Crude Gold Bars cannot fund investments or Bonds.

name: Duo and Five-Card
trait: Three tables: 15, 150 and 300 Silver buy-ins
summary: Two stick-card games. Duo plays at the Hernand inn for 15 Silver and at Tommaso for 300; Five-Card plays only at Beighen for 150. NeonLights reports the table AI calls reckless all-ins in the opening round. Watch cheaters three times to learn their trick, and accuse one mid-deal to take the pot.

return.basis: 400–600 Silver per winning Five-Card session at Beighen.

effort.basis: Played hand by hand.

setup.basis: A buy-in.

scale.basis: One table at a time, capped by its stakes.

steps: Learn the hands at the 15-Silver Hernand table, upstairs at the inn.
Go all in early on a strong opener; opponents tend to call.
Watch for the dealer's elbow-and-thumb tell and hold Accuse while they deal.
Move to Beighen's Five-Card or Tommaso's Duo once the bankroll covers losing streaks.

location: Hernand inn (Duo, 15); Beighen (Five-Card, 150); Tommaso (Duo, 300).
notes: Patch 2.03.01 fixed the Tommaso Duo dealers not appearing.

name: Sleep and Wait
trait: Every timer on this route runs on the in-game clock
summary: Dispatches, bank cycles, shipbuilding, castle rebuilds and island pioneering all count in-game hours. Sleeping or waiting at a campfire moves the clock forward, so every timer on the route finishes sooner. Fatigue gates sleep: you can only sleep again once it builds back up.

return.basis: Pays nothing itself; shortens every timer on this route.

effort.basis: A rest between other jobs.

setup.basis: Any bed, tent or campfire.

scale.basis: Applies to every timed system at once.

steps: Before resting, check every dispatch, crop, research task and build so one skip finishes several at once.
Sleep at a bed or tent, or wait at a campfire.
Collect, re-queue, and rest again when fatigue allows.

location: Any bed, tent or campfire.
notes: Sleeping just before a Repeat mission finishes can restart it before you collect; cancel the restarted run to recover its provisions.
